label: rem:dilog-saddle-regime
title: Dilog saddle regime: the $\theta = \pi/3$ saddle of $\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_2(e^{i\theta})$ and $\mathrm{Vol}(4_1)$
html:
Remark. Dilog saddle regime: the \theta = \pi/3 saddle of \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_2(e^{i\theta}) and \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)

The quasi-classical potential governing the Kashaev asymptotics of the figure-eight knot 4_1 is the imaginary part of the dilogarithm on the unit circle,

  V(\theta) \;=\; \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_2(e^{i\theta}),

the Clausen function \mathrm{Cl}_2(\theta) (Clausen function Mathlib filler). Its critical points solve

  \frac{d}{d\theta}\,\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_2(e^{i\theta})
  \;=\;
  -\log\bigl|2\sin(\theta/2)\bigr|
  \;=\; 0
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \bigl|2\sin(\theta/2)\bigr| = 1
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \theta = \frac{\pi}{3}.

Evaluating the potential at this root yields the hyperbolic volume of the regular ideal tetrahedron,

  V(\pi/3) \;=\; \mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3) \;\approx\; 1.01494,

and since the 4_1 complement is glued from two such tetrahedra,

  \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) \;=\; 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3) \;\approx\; 2.02988.

This saddle computation is the concrete 4_1 instance of the Kashaev volume conjecture asymptotics. Blocks that invoke the dilog saddle regime — the continuum c_3 geometry discussion, the \Phi_q/AJ machinery identification, and the q_0 Stokes-region identification — reference this derivation rather than repeating it.
